findings.description: The frozen contract explicitly requires the listed native-graph checks for every native fixture. The implementation tests provide meaningful coverage, but the stationary/Schur comparison runs only N_BRANCH3 and N_BRACED5, leaving N_RING4 and N_DISJOINT2 uncovered. Loaded covariance runs only N_BRACED5, and explicit shared-Q identity across incident elements is checked only for N_BRANCH3. Existing G1/G2 tests and the other G3a checks do not establish these missing graph-specific obligations.
findings.observed: The stationary/Schur test parametrization names only N_BRANCH3 and N_BRACED5. test_loaded_graph_covariance constructs N_BRACED5 exclusively. Explicit comparisons between each element's stored nodal rotations and the shared rotation store occur in test_three_arm_branch_smoke.
findings.required_change: Complete the frozen native-fixture coverage matrix, including stationary/Schur verification with nonzero internal residual for N_RING4 and N_DISJOINT2, physical covariance for the remaining native graphs, and explicit shared-pose/incident-triad checks wherever nodes have multiple incident elements. Preserve the registered equations, scales, tolerances and perturbation sequence.
findings.title: Complete the frozen per-graph S15 verification

findings.description: The graph transaction tests cover useful failure paths but do not fulfill the frozen rollback matrix. Last-element preparation rollback is exercised only on N_BRACED5, while cancellation is exercised on N_BRANCH3. The contract requires cancellation and last-element preparation rollback for every native graph. Additionally, the preregistered N_BRACED5 S18 oracle explicitly includes stale and foreign tokens, but the G3a test module contains no such token tests.
findings.gate: G3a native graph transaction and S18 token safety verification
findings.observed: test_last_element_prepare_failure_retains_complete_graph always constructs N_BRACED5. Cancellation checks construct the default N_BRANCH3 owner. No G3a test exercises stale or foreign issued tokens; the module's only occurrence of 'foreign' is a malformed checkpoint schema string.
findings.required_change: Add the missing per-graph cancellation/preparation rollback regressions and the frozen N_BRACED5 stale/foreign-token cases. Exercise genuine accepted prefixes and verify unchanged committed bytes, both generations, history and authenticated checkpoint, no residual trial, and continued replay. Keep supporting G1/G2 regression inventories separate.
findings.title: Complete the frozen graph rollback and token matrix

scope.coverage_assessment: The existing tests meaningfully cover all four reference graph/component inventories, rigid-space dimensions and positive quotient stiffness, sorted assembly, five-step loading/unloading, recovery and replay. They also exercise noncommuting targets, nonzero-multiplier directional derivatives, native remote-pose equivalence, preparation failure and selected mutations. The findings concern specific frozen obligations absent from that coverage, not evidence that the corresponding implementation paths necessarily fail.
scope.formal_confirmation: Not executed. No G3a formal confirmation runner exists in the reviewed candidate, and this review grants no runner acceptance. Complete scoped corrections and independent re-review, then freeze and independently review the exact formal runner and inventories before execution.
scope.implementation_assessment: The owner is an exact separate NativeGraphAnalysis, not a G1/G2 subclass or nested owner. Admission bounds graph incidence, midpoint ownership and supported component rigid spaces before model/state construction. One native rotation store owns shared poses. Constraint capture retains analytical G2 equations under separate graph bounds. The owner authenticates graph, DOF ordering, topology cache, store identities and scoped loads; material preparation reuses the inherited final authority check. G1/G2 solve dispatch is rejected by exact-type and entry-capability guards. Reference multi-RHS factorization is ephemeral and rejects accepted epochs. No additional demonstrated correctness defect was found in these inspected paths.
